title: Quiver for Ad-Hoc Counterparty Queries — Lightweight Investigator Tooling Without a Full Workshop Build
validation_scope: 5 Quiver queries cover the seed's worked example + 4 supplementary patterns; each query has target_object_class, filters, aggregations, visualization (primary + secondary primitives), parameters, share_link_default_permission, expected_runtime.
7-criterion graduation-criteria checklist with threshold rules and cost-of-getting-it-wrong analysis in each direction.

Audit-considerations doc captures the load-bearing regulatory framing: what Quiver activity logs capture / do not capture, the snapshot discipline bridging to Article 005's AuditEntry, mapping to SR 11-7 §V, FFIEC BSA/AML, PCAOB AS 2201.
Synthetic-data CSV summarizes the 5 queries' inputs, expected result shapes, runtime estimates, large-universe caveats.
Screenshot-equivalents render Quiver Instant-Query Mode, Query Result, Save-As-Parameterized, Share Link, Graduation-Criteria Self-Assessment.
known_limits: Portable companion bundle; YAML query specs require re-keying into Quiver UI to execute.
Quiver visualization rendering happens in the platform; screen-equivalents only show layout.
Graduation-criteria checklist is heuristic (4-of-7); institution-specific calibration may shift the threshold.
framing_discipline: Quiver is for one-off questions; Workshop (Article 003) is for repeated workflows. The bundle's editorial center is the decision framework + audit-trail bridge to Article 005, not a Quiver vendor pitch. Patterns transfer to Snowflake Streamlit-on-Snowflake and Databricks Lakeview with minor adjustments.
